status: published curve with unverified or cohort-specific tail

assessment ratio: Apply the separate 20% Class II assessment ratio after valuation.

source details: Manual pages 2, 24 and 40 establish the cost basis and computer classification. The October 2026 table supplies the factors and expressly prohibits indexing them again. The first October assessment can occur during the acquisition calendar year.

status: no single verified statewide original-cost curve
asset class: Ordinary movable business computer and server equipment.
source vintage: Current state municipal-tax guidance, checked November 2026.
authority: Municipal taxation and valuation under state statutes.
valuation basis: Local full and true value; no uniform statewide server curve.

assessment ratio: Local assessment practices apply.

source details: The Alaska DCRA property-tax guidance describes municipal authority under AS 29.45.010 and optional exemptions under AS 29.45.050. It does not establish a statewide acquisition-age schedule for ordinary data-center equipment.

asset class: Eligible locally assessed commercial computer and server hardware initially classified in 2022 or later.
source vintage: 2026 valuation manual and current A.R.S. 42-13054.
authority: Mandatory state statutory valuation.
valuation basis: 2.5% of acquisition cost in each assessment year.

eligibility and exceptions: Initial classification date and legal class determine eligibility. Legacy and centrally valued property require separate treatment.
source details: A.R.S. 42-13054(B)(4) establishes the special valuation. The 2026 manual assigns computers and peripherals to Table 5 and identifies eligible recent cohorts. This is a current-law curve for qualifying investment, not an unrestricted historical-vintage series.

asset class: Computers and equipment valued separately under the three-year schedule.
source vintage: 2024 Commercial Personal Property Appraisal Manual; schedules revised January 2021.
authority: State Assessment Coordination Division recommended guidelines.
valuation basis: Percent of historical acquisition cost.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: The three-year schedule reaches a 10% residual.
assessment ratio: Apply the separate 20% assessment ratio after valuation.
eligibility and exceptions: Appraiser judgment, asset condition and industry-level appraisal may affect the result.
source details: The alphabetical asset listing assigns computers and equipment to schedule 3. The remaining-economic-life table on printed page 128 gives 55%, 30% and 10%. These are appraisal guidelines; the source does not require identical values irrespective of actual market evidence.

asset class: LAN equipment and mainframes, expressly including servers; personal computers have a separate curve.

eligibility and exceptions: Factors provide mass-appraisal guidance and may be adjusted for supported market evidence.
source details: AH 581 pages 11–12 explain the historical-cost basis and server classification. The official 2026 data portal and API verify the LAN/mainframe factors. The substantially different personal-computer column is not used.

asset class: Class 4200, Computers Other, including servers, mainframes and standalone storage or peripheral equipment.
source vintage: 2026 state valuation tables and Assessors Reference Library, Volume 5.
authority: State valuation guidance applied by county assessors.
valuation basis: Percent of original cost; trend and level-of-value multipliers are both 1.00.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

assessment ratio: Apply the separate Colorado assessment rate after actual-value estimation.
eligibility and exceptions: Server hardware belongs to the four-year other-computer category; personal computers have a different life.
source details: The 2026 tables assign class 4200 to trend 1300, level-of-value 13A and depreciation 04a. The 04a factors are on page 6. Volume 5, pages 7.42–7.43, expressly identifies servers and the 7% floor.

asset class: Group I computer and peripheral hardware; the main series is conditional on that classification.
source vintage: Statutory schedules mandatory for assessment years beginning October 1, 2026.
authority: CGS 12-63(b)(3), as made mandatory by Public Act 26-114.
valuation basis: Percent of acquisition cost, including transportation and installation.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: Group I reaches 10% in year 4; Group II reaches 10% in year 5.
assessment ratio: Apply the separate 70% assessment ratio.
eligibility and exceptions: Servers are not expressly named. Group II other hardware, including mini/mainframe systems costing over $25,000, has a different curve. Qualified data-center agreements can provide exemptions.
source details: Section 10 of Public Act 26-114 removes the municipal option. The statute and Oxford’s 2026 notice distinguish Groups I and II. Confirm actual system classification before using the main series; the alternate Group II array is retained.

status: general exemption / no ordinary TPP tax
asset class: Ordinary movable computer and server personal property.
source vintage: Current 9 Del. C. § 8103, checked November 2026.
authority: State statutory prohibition on local tangible personal property taxes.
valuation basis: No ordinary taxable personal-property base.

terminal treatment: Zero denotes no ordinary TPP tax, not physical depreciation.
assessment ratio: Not applicable.
eligibility and exceptions: Real-property improvements are outside this treatment.
source details: Section 8103 prohibits counties, municipal corporations and other political subdivisions from taxing tangible personal property. There is no ordinary state ad valorem TPP levy in this baseline.

status: no single verified statewide original-cost curve
asset class: Mainframe and peripheral guidance uses a six-year life; PCs use four years.
source vintage: Currently posted 1997 guidelines; cost-index attachment updated January 15, 2026.
authority: Nonbinding state guidelines; county appraisers determine just value.
valuation basis: The reference percent-good curve applies to replacement cost new, not necessarily original cost.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

assessment ratio: Just value before applicable exemptions.
eligibility and exceptions: Counties may adopt other comparable tables. Cost trending may be inappropriate where technology replacement prices decline.
source details: Attachments C and D supply the raw six-year curve and asset lives. The introduction expressly states that these guidelines lack the force of rules. Their factors cannot be inserted into an original-cost comparison without resolving the cost index and local classification.

asset class: Group IV computer equipment in IRS asset class 00.12.

authority: Georgia Department of Revenue appraisal-procedures rules.

assessment ratio: Apply the separate 40% assessment ratio.
eligibility and exceptions: Supported physical, functional or economic obsolescence can justify adjustments. Project abatements are excluded.

status: general exemption / no ordinary TPP tax
asset class: Ordinary movable computer and server personal property.

asset class: Schedule 19 minicomputers, mainframes, servers and non-desktop peripherals; five-year life.
source vintage: 2026 appraisal guidelines, released April 30, 2026.

assessment ratio: Market-value factors before applicable exemptions.
eligibility and exceptions: The general per-county personal-property exemption and aggregation rules can affect liability. The separate small-computer schedule is not used.
source details: The workbook index and notes expressly assign servers to Schedule 19. On the personal-property page 15 worksheet, column W contains the verified composite factors. They should not be indexed a second time.

status: general exemption / no ordinary TPP tax
asset class: Ordinary commercial computer and server equipment.
source vintage: Current statute, checked November 2026.
authority: 35 ILCS 200/24-5 and Illinois Constitution, article IX, section 5.
valuation basis: No ad valorem personal-property tax base.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: Zero at every age indicates abolition of this tax.
assessment ratio: Not applicable.
eligibility and exceptions: Sales and use taxes and real-property taxes are separate.
source details: The statute prohibits ad valorem personal-property taxation. The constitutional provision required its abolition by 1979. Accordingly, no acquisition-age depreciation schedule is needed for ordinary data-center server personal property.

asset class: Computer and server equipment assigned five-year federal recovery life; Pool 2.
source vintage: 2026 DLGF instructions and tutorial.
authority: State regulation and prescribed return.
valuation basis: Pool factor multiplied by adjusted original federal tax cost.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: Pool 2 reaches 15% in year 7; a separate 30% aggregate floor can override this.
assessment ratio: No additional fractional assessment ratio.
eligibility and exceptions: The 30% floor generally remains for property placed in service by January 1, 2025, and specified existing TIF areas. Later investment generally avoids it. Actual local enterprise-IT exemptions are separate.
source details: The tutorial, page 10, confirms the intentional increase from 40% in year 1 to 56% in year 2. Pages 13–15 explain the floor exceptions. The series is the pool schedule, not a universal historical-cohort tax liability.

status: general exemption / no ordinary TPP tax
asset class: Ordinary movable computer and server personal property.
source vintage: Iowa Code 2026, § 427A.2.
authority: State statute.
valuation basis: No ordinary personal-property tax base.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: Zero denotes statutory non-taxation, not depreciation.
assessment ratio: Not applicable.
eligibility and exceptions: Certain attached improvements and fixtures are classified as real property under § 427A.1 and require separate analysis.
source details: Section 427A.2 states that personal property shall not be listed, assessed or taxed. The series concerns movable server hardware rather than the entire data-center facility.

asset class: Qualifying commercial or industrial equipment, including computers, acquired after June 30, 2006.
source vintage: 2026 Personal Property Valuation Guide and current K.S.A. 79-223.
authority: State statutory exemption.
valuation basis: Zero only for equipment satisfying the acquisition and eligibility rules.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: Eligible equipment is exempt irrespective of age.
assessment ratio: Legacy taxable equipment is subject to separate rules.
eligibility and exceptions: The zero row is conditional. Qualifying purchase, lease or entry into Kansas after the cutoff matters; some merger or reorganization transfers fail the acquisition test. Pre-cutoff equipment is not automatically exempt.
source details: The 2026 guide, printed page 67, explains the exemption. Kansas Commerce expressly includes computers and office equipment. This is general equipment law rather than a discretionary data-center incentive.

asset class: Class I integrated computer systems and peripherals, expressly including servers; five-year life.

authority: State prescribed valuation factors, with supported alternatives permitted.
valuation basis: Published composite conversion factor multiplied by original cost.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: 10% from year 5 onward; the table continues through age 13 and older.
assessment ratio: Full fair cash value before state and local tax rates.
eligibility and exceptions: The baseline excludes incentive-specific classifications and exemptions. Annual cost indexes can change the composite curve.
source details: Instructions page 8 identifies servers. The official Form 62A500 workbook, Schedule A cells C8:C12, verifies 82.8%, 50.8%, 30.7%, 19.5% and 10%; later cells remain 10%. The instructions define age 1 as acquisition in the preceding calendar year.

status: published curve with unverified or cohort-specific tail
asset class: Servers, mainframes and midrange computers; five-year life. PCs use a separate category.
source vintage: 2026 valuation tables; 2027 in Orleans Parish.
authority: Louisiana Tax Commission guidelines, with assessor discretion.
valuation basis: Composite cost-index and percent-good multiplier applied to acquisition cost.

assessment ratio: Apply the separate 15% assessment ratio.

source details: Chapter 25, § 2501D, explains the frozen multiplier. Table 2503A assigns servers five years; Table 2503C gives raw percent good. Updated Table 2503D appears in the December 2025 Louisiana Register, page 2008. Supported obsolescence adjustments remain possible.

asset class: Business servers potentially eligible for the Business Equipment Tax Exemption (BETE).
source vintage: Bulletin 28, September 23, 2025; current review in November 2026.
authority: State statutory exemption; local valuation for noneligible equipment.
valuation basis: Zero only if BETE eligibility and filing requirements are met.

terminal treatment: Eligible equipment is fully exempt; otherwise no uniform statewide computer curve applies.
assessment ratio: Municipal assessment ratios are separate for taxable property.
eligibility and exceptions: The zero row is conditional. Equipment must generally first enter Maine service after April 1, 2007, with first assessment in 2008 or later. Annual claims are required; utilities, telecommunications property and other exclusions matter.
source details: Bulletin 28, pages 2–3 and following, describes business use, federal-depreciation eligibility, timing and exclusions. Confirm the server’s classification and owner before assuming the exemption.

asset class: Category D data-processing and computer-based equipment; certain large mainframes are Category B.
source vintage: 2026 Form 1 instructions and current COMAR.
authority: State assessment regulation and SDAT instructions.
valuation basis: Original cost less 30 percentage points annually, with a 5% minimum.

terminal treatment: Category D reaches 5% in year 4.
assessment ratio: Apply local tax rates and exemptions after valuation.
eligibility and exceptions: Mainframes originally costing at least $500,000 use Category B: 20 percentage points annually, with a 10% minimum. The alternative array is retained.
source details: The 2026 depreciation chart on printed page 5 and COMAR 18.03.01.02 distinguish these subclasses. A data-center sales-tax exemption does not itself establish a property-tax exemption.

status: no single verified statewide original-cost curve
asset class: Revenue-producing server machinery in a data-center service business.

assessment ratio: Full fair cash value before local tax rates and exemptions.

status: general exemption / no ordinary TPP tax

source vintage: Current official guidance, checked November 2026.

year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

asset class: Computers and data-processing equipment; five-year economic life, with no trend.
source vintage: 2026 Business Personal Property Valuation Schedule.
authority: State Tax Commission guide under 68 O.S. 2875(A)(4).
valuation basis: Percent of original cost; no computer cost index applied.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

assessment ratio: Apply the county’s separate personal-property assessment ratio.
eligibility and exceptions: The schedules approximate fair cash value. Condition and functional or economic obsolescence can justify adjustments.
source details: Section X, PDF page 115, gives the five-year percent-good column. PDF page 118 assigns computers and data-processing equipment five years and specifies no trend. The introduction states that the guidelines are not absolute values.

asset class: Data-processing equipment and mainframes, expressly including servers; seven-year life.
source vintage: 2026 Personal Property Valuation Guidelines, revised November 18, 2025.
authority: Oregon Department of Revenue recommended procedures.
valuation basis: Percent of original cost new.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

assessment ratio: Property-tax rates and exemptions apply separately.

source details: Printed page 33 expressly provides the server/mainframe schedule; Table 2 on page 7 agrees. The guidance states that equipment available for use should not fall below the lowest published factor.

asset class: Class I computers, expressly including mainframes, servers and computer peripherals.
source vintage: Current statute, checked November 2026; classification amended in 2021.
valuation basis: Original purchase cost, including freight and installation; trending is prohibited.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

assessment ratio: The statutory factors determine assessed value before exemptions and local tax rates.

source details: Subsections (a)–(c) establish the cost basis, 95%, 80%, 60%, 30% and 20% Class I factors, continuing floor, and explicit server classification.

status: no single verified statewide original-cost curve
asset class: Ordinary business computer and server equipment reported as business personal property.
source vintage: Current SCDOR guidance and 2026 PT-300 instructions.
authority: State business-personal-property rules; return classification matters.
valuation basis: Capitalized cost less South Carolina income-tax depreciation.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

assessment ratio: Ordinary BPP uses a separate 10.5% assessment ratio.
eligibility and exceptions: Manufacturing or process-related equipment may use different categories. Fee-in-lieu agreements and other project incentives are excluded.
source details: SCDOR filing guidance caps depreciation at 90% of cost. PT-300 distinguishes gross-cost and net-book reporting schedules. A generic federal MACRS assumption is not substituted for actual South Carolina treatment. NA means no unique original-cost curve, not exemption.

assessment ratio: Apply the separate 30% commercial assessment ratio and any applicable equalization adjustment.

source details: Appendix A, PDF page 27, gives 67% for the most recent acquisition year, 33% for the next and 20% for earlier years. Appendix B, PDF page 31, identifies computer and network equipment. January 1 is the assessment date.

status: no single verified statewide original-cost curve
asset class: Ordinary taxable business computer and server personal property.
source vintage: Current Tax Code § 23.01 and HCAD’s 2026 local valuation guide.
authority: Local appraisal districts under a statewide market-value standard.
valuation basis: Local market-value appraisal; no uniform statewide original-cost schedule.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.

asset class: Mainframe and network computers, expressly including servers, storage and rack-mounted equipment.
source vintage: January 1, 2026 guidelines, published December 2025.
authority: State Department of Revenue recommended county valuation guidance.
valuation basis: Combined Trend II/N factor applied to original cost.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: 5% from year 11 onward; the published table continues through age 50.
assessment ratio: 100% current market value; no second cost trend should be added.
eligibility and exceptions: Physical server racks have another classification. Supported appraisal evidence may justify different values.
source details: The equipment index assigns network servers to Trend II/N. The original DOCX’s embedded combined-table workbook, column labeled N, verifies all factors. They already combine price trends and depreciation, so the raw declining-balance percentage alone would understate or overstate the published conversion.

asset class: Servers used directly in a qualifying high-technology business.
source vintage: Current W. Va. Code chapter 11, article 6J; checked November 2026.
authority: Special statutory valuation, requiring written county-assessor eligibility determination.
valuation basis: 5% of original cost, irrespective of equipment age.
year convention: Year 0 is a 100% acquisition-cost normalization for taxable or potentially taxable rows, not an actual assessment-year factor. Year 1 is the first assessment-age bucket; lien dates vary. Zero-coded exemption rows have year 0=0.
terminal treatment: 5% in every qualifying assessment year.
assessment ratio: Apply the separate 60% assessment ratio; ordinarily 3% of original cost becomes the assessed base.
eligibility and exceptions: Eligibility is essential. The business definition includes qualifying electronic data processing and network management; ordinary computers in unrelated businesses are not automatically covered.
source details: Sections 11-6J-2 through 11-6J-4 define the 5% value, covered server use and written determination. This is preferential statutory valuation rather than economic depreciation.
